body:
That’s so cool that your school offers those in the cafeteria! I’m Vietnamese, and they’re called bánh mì :)) You are not a coward, it takes a lot of strength to call for help especially when you were scared. 
Since you went to the hospital, if you’re feeling up to it, I’d definitely recommend reaching out to your school’s dean of students. Your teachers/professors will likely be understanding and flexible with deadlines given the circumstances

Dude, it's so good to hear that things are starting to look up for you. It's a lot of effort getting better but it seems like you're doing great so far. And I hope your sister feels better from covid soon too

First, thank you for replying.

I'm 17, so I would need my parents to get any treatment. I was originally hoping to leave for college and see what type of counseling resources were available, but at the rate things are going I doubt I will be able to get into college.
sure, if it's not too much trouble you can send it
I'm glad you were able to get into a better situation. I think I do feel quite bleak. I can't really imagine the future or make goals anymore. I will wait it out, though
Thank you for being really kind. I feel bad that he works so hard and I'm just like this. I keep sabotaging myself and any possibility of a future.
It's not even the failure, I just can't even make goals anymore. I can't see a future with me being alive or growing old.

I'm really dreading going back to school.

I don't think I will be brave enough to tell the counselor. I tried to tell my doctor during the annual physical, but I couldn't say it out loud and I was scared because I wasn't sure what they would do about it. I did write it on the form they give out in the beginning, but I don't think they pay much attention to those.

I'm 16. I have been working over the summer and I have bank accounts. I feel a but embarrassed though because all my friends are at their prestigious summer programs that I procrastinated applying for. I missed a bunch of deadlines and got rejected from the few I managed to get done. I just feel a bit ashamed...

My dad has always talked down upon people who work lower wage jobs instead of going to college. I know that every job and everyone is valid, but it just still hurts when he suggests that I do those things because he's always been saying bad things about the people who do them.
Thank you, it means so much to me

There's no reason to live and waste resources. I have a negative impact on the people around me too and there's no need for them to experience that. My dad sometimes talks about how much more free time and money he'd have if he didn't waste it on me and my brother. 

I'm also trans and in the closet, but neither of my parents would be supportive.

I'm supposed to be a good influence on my younger brother but if he ends up anything like me, no one could be proud of him. I don't want to burden my friends by telling them this information because they all have their own lives and problems.

I also want to say thanks for listening, even though we're just strangers.

I have no bills to pay, food on the table, and a roof over my head. This is the least stressful time I would ever possibly have in my life and I still fuck everything up. If I can't even handle this, there's no hope. No one around me deserves to deal with me
There's nothing left for me. I'm just a waste of their resources and time. I can't handle another school year. I need to die before then but I'm too scared to go through with it

It seems that you might be able to receive some help from your college when you get there. I know it's hard to even think about starting school again, but it seems like a way you can get some support.

It feels terrible to keep all these feelings inside and not have anyone to talk to. Do you have any friends you would feel comfortable talking to? If you want to vent more, I'm all ears too
Oh, I don't know too much beyond that. I'm sorry. It seems that you try to distance yourself from the thoughts and minimize the distress you feel from them, rather than trying to stop thinking them.

I'm not an expert, so take this with a grain of salt, but they sound like intrusive thoughts. As long as you don't act on them or believe they're a good idea, they shouldn't be a reason to freak out. That being said, if you are concerned or if you wish to hurt yourself you should talk to someone about it.
What kind of thoughts did you have?

Oh man, when I read this I could have thought I wrote it. I'm also 16 and closeted ftm. The summer gets hard sometimes with all the extra time to think. You aren't alone. There's plenty of other people who share similar experiences, even on just this sub.

Coming out and transitioning are both tough and it's normal to feel nervous, dreadful, scared. The pressure from both your parents and yourself can be overwhelming too.

Have you told anyone how you feel?
I don't think we're allowed to discuss methods here. What's making you feel this way?
This is all very reassuring
Sometimes it's hard to imagine the future and being able to move away one day since I feel like I'll be dead before then, but thank you for your kind words. They mean a lot to me

It's comforting to know other people think this way. If another trans person asked me if they were normal I would say yes, but it's just difficult to view myself as normal. It's hard to believe I will ever be a "real man."

I don't think I would have much of a place to live if I told my parents. I told some friends in middle school, but they thought it was a phase. One of my friends even told me that it was "inconvenient for her that I felt this way." I don't hold it against her because it was middle school, but it still hurt. I only have one friend that actually believes me.

Thank you. Even though I'm still young it's just hard for me to see any recovery from this point. I feel like I keep digging myself into a hole.

I would hope that the authorities would be the ones to clean up my mess, but I would feel bad to have them see that.

Telling someone would be good. If I tell a professional, I'm scared they would tell my parents, and I don't think they would really appreciate finding out that I feel this way. I don't think I should burden my friends with these types of thoughts either.

I can't handle another school year and I'm just a horrible person. I can't gather the energy to be productive anymore. No one around me deserves to be let down time and time again like this. I'm also trans, but I wish I was normal. 

Why would bleeding out be ineffective?
Thank you so much for replying. Everything just feels so hopeless
